neighbours.label: the substitute choice when the context sets up a replacement (what to use instead, who to send in someone's place); output promotes 'instead'/'rather'
fire: If you can't eat wheat, what should you use for the pie crust?
The bakery had no rye left, so she bought sourdough instead.
He couldn't attend the meeting and sent his deputy in his place.
If you don't own a drill, what tool should you use?
The road was closed, so they took the coastal route instead.
Since the hall was booked, the club chose to meet in the library.
When the milk ran out, we used water in the batter instead.
She turned down the role and recommended her colleague for it.
quiet: When you bake a pie, what should you put in the crust first?
The bakery had fresh rye this morning, so she bought two loaves.
He attended the meeting and took notes for his deputy.
If you own a drill, you can hang the shelf in a few minutes.
The road was open, so they drove along the coast to the village.
The club meets every Thursday evening in the library.
We mixed the milk and eggs into the batter and let it rest.
She accepted the role and thanked her colleague for the advice.

notes: Top examples: 'what should you buy?' after 'do not buy stew meat', 'suggested X in his stead', 'was used instead'. Probe: 'what should you drink?' 0.55 after 'If you don't like coffee', 0.03 without it. Near misses keep the topic and drop the replacement setup.
